newsitem.title: SPAIN: French strike increases air space demand ex-Spain.
newsitem.headline: French strike increases air space demand ex-Spain.

text.p: The strike by French truck drivers has prompted greater interest in air cargo flights to the U.K. and is forcing carriers like Lufthansa to fly rather than drive Spanish origin cargo to Germany, airlines said.
British Airways reported a flood of enquiries about rates for flying perishable goods to the U.K. but said so far few had resulted in actual bookings.
"People are asking us about taking perishable products to London, something we've never done before," a British Airways cargo official said.
"There are a lot of enquiries but not much is turning into business. If half the calls resulted in bookings we'd be out of space."

Air France said it was not seeing extra business, but added that it flies only narrowbody aircraft from Spain to France and therefore could not accommodate most of the loads that habitually went by truck to Paris.
But Lufthansa said demand for air cargo to many destinations was sharply higher in Spain.
"We're seeing an increase in requests for perishables and other goods to Germany, Scandinavia and Eastern Europe and also to France via Germany," a cargo salesman said.
The airline was also flying much of its regular Spanish origin cargo to Germany instead of sending it by road as it usually did, he added.
"This will probably increase if the strike goes on," he added.
The daily newspaper El Pais said fruit and vegetable growers in Spain were slowing their harvest because of the blockade of French roads.

Spain exported 6.4 million tonnes of fresh fruit and vegetables to other European Union countries last year, much of it in the November to January period, it said. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
